# Define the ordinal columns

# Convert these columns to ordered factors with levels 0 to 3

})

```{r}
# Step 1: Select the relevant columns
scale_columns <- dplyr::select(scale_data, all_of(ordinal_cols))

# Step 2: Calculate the proportion of NA values in each row
na_proportion <- rowSums(is.na(scale_columns)) / ncol(scale_columns)

# Step 3: Filter rows where more than 60% of the values are NA
rows_with_more_than_60_percent_na <- scale_data[na_proportion > 0.6, ]

# View the result
print(rows_with_more_than_60_percent_na)
```

```{r}
scale_data_clean <- scale_data[na_proportion <= 0.6, ]
```

```{r}
# Count total number of NAs in the entire dataframe
total_NAs <- sum(is.na(scale_data_clean))
print(total_NAs)
```

```{r}
# Your ordinal variable names
ordinal_vars <- ordinal_cols

# Create the method vector
method_vector <- rep("logreg", ncol(scale_data_clean))
names(method_vector) <- names(scale_data_clean)

method_vector[ordinal_vars] <- "polr"  # Set ordinal variables to "polr"

# Instead of "polr", you can try "pmm" (Predictive Mean Matching), which is less computationally demanding
# method_vector[ordinal_vars] <- "pmm"

# Exclude 'subjectkey' - CORRECTED
predictorMatrix <- matrix(1, nrow = ncol(scale_data_clean), ncol = ncol(scale_data_clean))
diag(predictorMatrix) <- 0

# Set row and column names of predictorMatrix to match data frame
rownames(predictorMatrix) <- colnames(scale_data_clean)
colnames(predictorMatrix) <- colnames(scale_data_clean)

predictorMatrix["subjectkey", ] <- 0  
predictorMatrix[, "subjectkey"] <- 0

# Perform imputation
set.seed(123)
imputed_data <- mice(scale_data_clean, 
                     method = method_vector, 
                     m = 1,
                     predictorMatrix = predictorMatrix)
```

```{r}
imputed_first <- complete(imputed_data, 1)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
# Define the BAPQ variable names
scale_vars <- c(
    "dass_p2_1", "dass_p1_2", "dass_p1_3", "dass_p2_1", "dass_p1_2", "dass_p1_3", "dass_p1_4", "dass_p2_21", "dass_p1_6", "dass_p2_20", 
  "dass_p1_12", "dass_p2_19", "dass_p1_10", "dass_p2_18", "dass_p1_8", "dass_p2_5", "dass_p2_14", "dass_p2_7", "dass_p2_10", 
  "dass_p1_17", "dass_p1_18", "dass_p2_4", "dass_p1_20", "dass_p2_17", "dass_depr_sc", "dass_anx_sc", "dass_stress_sc", 
  "dass_p1_1", "dass_p2_2", "dass_p2_3", "dass_p1_19", "dass_p1_13", "dass_p2_6", "dass_p1_15", "dass_p2_8", "dass_p2_9", 
  "dass_p1_16", "dass_p2_11", "dass_p2_12", "dass_p2_13", "dass_p1_14", "dass_p2_15", "dass_p2_16", "dass_p1_21", 
  "dass_p1_11", "dass_p1_9", "dass_p1_7", "dass_p1_5"
)


scale_data_clean[scale_vars] <- lapply(scale_data_clean[scale_vars], as.numeric)
imputed_first[scale_vars] <- lapply(imputed_first[scale_vars], as.numeric)



# Convert the original data to long format
orig_long <- scale_data_clean[, scale_vars] %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Scale_Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  count(Scale_Variable, Value) %>%
  mutate(Source = "Original")

# Convert the imputed data to long format
imp_long <- imputed_first[, scale_vars] %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Scale_Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
  count(Scale_Variable, Value) %>%
  mutate(Source = "Imputed")

# Combine the counts
combined_counts <- bind_rows(orig_long, imp_long)

# Loop over each variable and create a separate plot
for(var in unique(combined_counts$Scale_Variable)) {
  p <- ggplot(filter(combined_counts, Scale_Variable == var),
              aes(x = Value, y = n, fill = Source)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    labs(title = paste("Distribution of", var, "(Original vs. Imputed)"),
         x = "Value",
         y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  print(p)  # In RStudio, each plot will be rendered sequentially in the Plots pane.
}

```
